title: In a reduced ring the zerodivisors are the union of the minimal primes
statement: Let $R$ be a reduced commutative ring (no nonzero nilpotent elements). Call $x\in R$ a zerodivisor if $xy=0$ for some $y\in R$, $y\neq0$. Then the set of zerodivisors of $R$ equals the union $\bigcup_{\mathfrak p}\mathfrak p$ of all minimal prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ (prime ideals containing no strictly smaller prime ideal). In particular a nonzerodivisor of $R$ lies in no minimal prime, and an element lying in no minimal prime is a nonzerodivisor.

mathlib_searches.query: in a reduced ring the union of the minimal primes is the set of zero divisors
every zero divisor of a reduced commutative ring lies in some minimal prime ideal
